arxiv-2101-04607.title: When is settling important for particle concentrations in wall-bounded turbulent flows?
arxiv-2101-04607.creator: A.D. Bragg, D. H. Richter, G. Wang
arxiv-2101-04607.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by A.D. Bragg, D. H. Richter, G. Wang. We explore the role of gravitational settling on inertial particle concentrations in a wall-bounded turbulent flow. While it may be thought that settling can be ignored when the settling parameter S ​ v ≡ v s / u τ Sv\equiv v_{s}/u_{\tau} is small ( v s v_{s} - Stokes settling velocity, u τ u_{\tau} - fluid friction velocity), we show that even in this regime the settling may make a leading order contribution to the concentration profiles.

arxiv-2201-05306.title: Maximal L p L_{p} - L q L_{q} regularity for the Stokes equations with various boundary conditions in the half space
arxiv-2201-05306.creator: Naoto Kajiwara
arxiv-2201-05306.description: Abstract We prove resolvent L p L_{p} estimates and maximal L p L_{p} - L q L_{q} regularity estimates for the Stokes equations with Dirichlet, Neumann and Robin boundary conditions in the half space. Each solution is constructed by a Fourier multiplier of x ′ x^{\prime} -direction and an integral of x N x_{N} -direction.

arxiv-2202-13629.title: Local strict singular characteristics II: existence for stationary equation on ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2}
arxiv-2202-13629.creator: Wei Cheng and Jiahui Hong
arxiv-2202-13629.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Wei Cheng and Jiahui Hong. The notion of strict singular characteristics is important in the wellposedness issue of singular dynamics on the cut locus of the viscosity solutions. We provide an intuitive and rigorous proof of the existence of the strict singular characteristics of Hamilton-Jacobi equation H ⁡ ( x , D ​ u ​ ( x ) , u ⁡ ( x ) ) = 0 H(x,Du(x),u(x))=0 in two dimensional case.

arxiv-2206-00957.title: Conjugate Connections and their Applications on Pure Metallic Metric Geometries
arxiv-2206-00957.creator: Olgun DURMAZ, Aydin GEZER
arxiv-2206-00957.description: Abstract . Let ( M , J , g ) \left(M,J,g\right) be a metallic pseudo-Riemannian manifold equipped with a metallic structure J J and a pseudo-Riemannian metric g g . The paper deals with interactions of Codazzi couplings formed by conjugate connections and tensor structures.

C20/IS/14767486
arxiv-2206-12217.creator: Mirza Golam Kibria 1 , , Hayder Al-Hraishawi 2 , , Eva Lagunas 2 , , Symeon Chatzinotas 2 , , and Björn Ottersten 2 , , 1 Department of Research and Development, Huawei, Stockholm, Sweden
arxiv-2206-12217.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mirza Golam Kibria 1 , , Hayder Al-Hraishawi 2 , , Eva Lagunas 2 , , Symeon Chatzinotas 2 , , and Björn Ottersten 2 , , 1 Department of Research and Development, Huawei, Stockholm, Sweden. Beam hopping (BH) and carrier aggregation (CA) are two promising technologies for the next generation satellite communication systems to achieve several orders of magnitude increase in system capacity and to significantly improve the spectral efficiency.

arxiv-2210-08642.title: Data-Efficient Pipeline for Offline Reinforcement Learning with Limited Data
arxiv-2210-08642.creator: Allen NieYannis Flet-BerliacDeon R. Jordan William SteenbergenEmma Brunskill Department of Computer ScienceStanford University* anie@stanford.edu
arxiv-2210-08642.description: Abstract Offline reinforcement learning (RL) can be used to improve future performance by leveraging historical data. There exist many different algorithms for offline RL, and it is well recognized that these algorithms, and their hyperparameter settings, can lead to decision policies with substantially differing performance.

arxiv-2306-11965.title: Symmetry’s Edge in Cortical Dynamics Multiscale Dynamics of Ensemble Excitation and Inhibition
arxiv-2306-11965.creator: Nima Dehghani
arxiv-2306-11965.description: Abstract Creating a quantitative theory for the cortex presents challenges and raises questions. What are the significant scales–micro, meso, or macroscopic? What are the interactions–pairwise, higher order, or mean-field? And what control parameters are relevant–noisy, dissipative, or emergent? We suggest an approach inspired by advances in understanding matter.

arxiv-2310-12125.title: Comprehensive High-resolution Chemical Spectroscopy of Barnard’s star with SPIRou Facilities: CFHT/SPIRou Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) ; matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) ; SciPy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 ) ; NumPy ( Harris et al. 2020 )
arxiv-2310-12125.creator: Farbod Jahandar, René Doyon, Étienne Artigau, Neil J. Cook, Charles Cadieux, David Lafrenière, Thierry Forveille, Jean-François Donati, Pascal Fouqué, Andrés Carmona, Ryan Cloutier, Paul Cristofari, Eric Gaidos, João Gomes da Silva, Lison Malo, Eder Martioli, J.-D. do Nascimento, Jr, Stefan Pelletie
arxiv-2310-12125.description: Abstract Determination of fundamental parameters of stars impacts all fields of astrophysics, from galaxy evolution to constraining the internal structure of exoplanets. This paper presents a detailed spectroscopic analysis of Barnard’s star that compares an exceptionally high-quality (an average signal-to-noise ratio of ∼ \sim 1000 in the entire domain), high-resolution NIR spectrum taken with CFHT/SPIRou to PHOENIX-ACES stellar atmosphere models.

arxiv-2312-05541.title: DPoser: Diffusion Model as Robust 3D Human Pose Prior
arxiv-2312-05541.creator: Junzhe Lu, Jing Lin, Hongkun Dou, Yulun Zhang, Yue Deng, Haoqian Wang
arxiv-2312-05541.description: Abstract Modeling human pose is a cornerstone in applications from human-robot interaction to augmented reality, yet crafting a robust human pose prior remains a challenge due to biomechanical constraints and diverse human movements. Traditional priors like VAEs and NDFs often fall short in realism and generalization, especially in extreme conditions such as unseen noisy poses.

arxiv-2401-04181.title: Language-Conditioned Robotic Manipulation with Fast and Slow Thinking
arxiv-2401-04181.creator: Minjie Zhu, Yichen Zhu, Jinming Li, Junjie Wen, Zhiyuan Xu, Zhengping Che, Chaomin Shen, Yaxin Peng, Dong Liu, Feifei Feng, Jian Tang
arxiv-2401-04181.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Minjie Zhu, Yichen Zhu, Jinming Li, Junjie Wen, Zhiyuan Xu, Zhengping Che, Chaomin Shen, Yaxin Peng, Dong Liu, Feifei Feng, Jian Tang. The language-conditioned robotic manipulation aims to transfer natural language instructions into executable actions, from simple “pick-and-place” to tasks requiring intent recognition and visual reasoning.

arxiv-2404-12396.title: Optimized Dynamic Mode Decomposition for Reconstruction and Forecasting of Atmospheric Chemistry Data
arxiv-2404-12396.creator: Meghana Velegar 1 , Christoph Keller 2,3 and J. Nathan Kutz 1,4
arxiv-2404-12396.description: Abstract We introduce the optimized dynamic mode decomposition algorithm for constructing an adaptive and computationally efficient reduced order model and forecasting tool for global atmospheric chemistry dynamics. By exploiting a low-dimensional set of global spatio-temporal modes, interpretable characterizations of the underlying spatial and temporal scales can be computed.

arxiv-2405-11833.title: Determination of the Néel vector in rutile altermagnets through x-ray magnetic circular dichroism: the case of MnF 2
arxiv-2405-11833.creator: A. Hariki, T. Okauchi, Y. Takahashi, J. Kuneš
arxiv-2405-11833.description: Abstract We present a numerical simulation of x-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) at the L 2 , 3 L_{2,3} edge of Mn in a representative rutile altermagnet MnF 2 using a combination of density functional theory + exact diagonalization of the atomic model.

arxiv-2410-21421.title: Breaking the north-south symmetry: dyonic spinning black holes with synchronized gauged scalar hair
arxiv-2410-21421.creator: Pedro V. P. Cunha, Carlos A. R. Herdeiro, Eugen Radu, Nuno M. Santos
arxiv-2410-21421.description: Abstract We study stationary clouds of a gauged, complex scalar field on a magnetically (and possibly electrically as well) charged Kerr-Newman black hole (BH). The existence of a magnetic charge Q m Q_{m} promotes a north-south asymmetry of the scalar clouds.

arxiv-2505-12226.title: Shallow Flow Matching for Coarse-to-Fine Text-to-Speech Synthesis
arxiv-2505-12226.creator: Dong Yang, Yiyi Cai, Yuki Saito, Lixu Wang, Hiroshi Saruwatari
arxiv-2505-12226.description: Abstract We propose Shallow Flow Matching (SFM), a novel mechanism that enhances flow matching (FM)-based text-to-speech (TTS) models within a coarse-to-fine generation paradigm. Unlike conventional FM modules, which use the coarse representations from the weak generator as conditions, SFM constructs intermediate states along the FM paths from these representations.

arxiv-2510-18745.title: Topoformer: brain-like topographic organization in Transformer language models through spatial querying and reweighting
arxiv-2510-18745.creator: Taha Binhuraib, Greta Tuckute, Nicholas M. Blauch
arxiv-2510-18745.description: Abstract Spatial functional organization is a hallmark of biological brains: neurons are arranged topographically according to their response properties, at multiple scales. In contrast, representations within most machine learning models lack spatial biases, instead manifesting as disorganized vector spaces that are difficult to visualize and interpret.

arxiv-2511-06628.title: Stochastic Optimal Impulse Controls with Changing Running Costs
arxiv-2511-06628.creator: Yuchen Cao and Jiongmin Yong
arxiv-2511-06628.description: Abstract Abstract. This paper is concerned with stochastic impulse control problems in which the running cost changes depending on the impulse control. Because of such a dependence, it brings several difficulties when the usual dynamic programming principle is to be used. The corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation (a quasi-variational inequality) is derived, which contains a parameter.

arxiv-2511-15682.title: Quantum measurement tomography with mini-batch stochastic gradient descent
arxiv-2511-15682.creator: Akshay Gaikwad, Manuel Sebastian Torres, Anton Frisk Kockum
arxiv-2511-15682.description: Abstract Drawing inspiration from gradient-descent methods developed for data processing in quantum state tomography [ Quantum Sci. Technol. 10 045055 (2025) ] and quantum process tomography [ Phys. Rev. Lett. 130 , 150402 (2023) ], we introduce stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithms for fast quantum measurement tomography (QMT), applicable to both discrete- and continuous-variable quantum systems—thus completing the tomography trio.

arxiv-2602-10435.title: Multiconfiguration Pair-Density Functional Theory Calculations of Ground and Excited States of Complex Chemical Systems with Quantum Computers
arxiv-2602-10435.creator: Zhanou Liu, Yuhao Chen, Yingjin Ma, Xiao He, Yuxin Deng
arxiv-2602-10435.description: Abstract Accurately describing strong electron correlation in complex systems remains a prominent challenge in computational chemistry as near-term quantum algorithms treating total correlation often require prohibitively deep circuits. Here we present a hybrid strategy combining the Variational Quantum Eigensolver with Multiconfiguration Pair-Density Functional Theory to efficiently decouple correlation effects.

pmc-10577295.title: Update on stomata development and action under abiotic stress
pmc-10577295.creator: Hubert Matkowski, Agata Daszkowska-Golec
pmc-10577295.description: Stomata, key gatekeepers of plant hydration, have long been known to play a pivotal role in mitigating the impacts of abiotic stressors. However, the complex molecular mechanisms underscoring this role remain unresolved fully and continue to be the subject of research.

pmc-10666241.title: Selection of the Second Adsorbent for Sampling Volatile Organic Compounds in the Biomass Gasification Tar Using Solid-Phase Adsorption
pmc-10666241.creator: Aleksandrs Pučkins, Sergejs Osipovs
pmc-10666241.description: The purpose of this study is to examine the effectiveness of a solid-phase adsorption method for measuring the concentrations of tar compounds in biomass. This method involves collecting tars on a column with an amino-phase sorbent. However, because biomass tar has a high concentration of volatile organic compounds, not all of them can be collected with just one column.

pmc-10695948.title: Contact with nature for emotion regulation: the roles of nature connectedness and beauty engagement in urban young adults
pmc-10695948.creator: Xuan Gu, Hailin Zheng, Chi-Shing Tse
pmc-10695948.description: Contact with nature has emotional benefits, but the psychological mechanism and potential moderator underlying the association between nature contact and emotion regulation remain unclear. The present study investigated how self-reported frequency of nature contact is associated with the use of emotion regulation strategies and explored the mediating role of nature connectedness (i.e.

pmc-10922929.title: Liquid application dosing alters the physiology of air-liquid interface (ALI) primary human bronchial epithelial cell/lung fibroblast co-cultures and in vitro testing relevant endpoints
pmc-10922929.creator: Nicholas M. Mallek, Elizabeth M. Martin, Lisa A. Dailey, Shaun D. McCullough
pmc-10922929.description: Differentiated primary human bronchial epithelial cell (dpHBEC) cultures grown under air-liquid interface (ALI) conditions exhibit key features of the human respiratory tract and are thus critical for respiratory research as well as efficacy and toxicity testing of inhaled substances (e.g., consumer products, industrial chemicals, and pharmaceuticals). Many inhalable substances (e.g.

pmc-11300980.title: Peripheral artery disease recognition, diagnosis, and management in general practice in the Republic of Ireland and England: an online survey
pmc-11300980.creator: Judit Konya, Sinead TJ McDonagh, Peter Hayes, Sebastian Debus, Victor Aboyans, Christopher E Clark, for the EuroPAD investigators
pmc-11300980.description: BackgroundPeripheral artery disease (PAD) is common and associated with future cardiovascular events. PAD is underdiagnosed, which limits opportunities to address secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease. It is unknown how closely guidelines for detection of PAD are followed in primary care.AimTo survey GPs’ attitudes to diagnosis and follow-up of patients with PAD.

pmc-11417224.title: Breeding biology of Great White Pelican Pelecanus onocrotalus at Lake Tana, Ethiopia
pmc-11417224.creator: Ahmed Yesuf Yimer, Shimelis Aynalem Zelelew, Mezgebu Ashagrie, Azmeraw Alemkere, Aschalew Alelign
pmc-11417224.description: Great White Pelicans, once thriving at Lake Shala, have faced a decline in breeding pairs at Lake Abijata due to increased salinity and overfishing. A study at Lake Tana Biosphere, from December 2020 to December 2021, aimed to understand their breeding biology, which had not been previously documented.

pmc-11656188.title: Tetracarpidium conophorum nuts (African walnuts) up‐regulated adiponectin and PPAR‐γ expressions with reciprocal suppression of TNF‐α gene in obesity
pmc-11656188.creator: Grace Ufedo Umoru, Item Justin Atangwho, Esien David‐Oku, Daniel Ejim Uti, Eyuwa Ignatius Agwupuye, Uket Nta Obeten, Swastika Maitra, Vetriselvan Subramaniyan, Ling Shing Wong, Nada H Aljarba, Vinoth Kumarasamy
pmc-11656188.description: Tetracarpidium conophorum nuts are nutrient‐dense Nigerian snacks associated with weight regulation. This study explores the nuts' impact on adipose tissue gene expression associated with low‐grade inflammation. Ethanol whole extract (EWE), ethyl‐acetate fraction (EAF) and the resulting residue (RES) were orally administered once daily to MSG‐induced obese rats for 6 weeks (n = 6).

pmc-12542392.title: Nurses’ roles and responsibilities in suicide prevention: a scoping review
pmc-12542392.creator: Annette Riedel, Stephanie Feinauer, Erik Jacob, Pia Madeleine Haug, Karen Klotz, Thomas Heidenreich
pmc-12542392.description: BackgroundGlobally, suicide remains a major public health concern. As frontline caregivers, nurses play a crucial role in identifying and supporting those at risk. Despite their central role, the specific contribution of nurses to suicide prevention across the suicide prevention continuum and various care settings has not been mapped comprehensively.

pmc-13194282.title: Qualitative perspectives of early surgeon users on the value of the daVinci 5 surgical system
pmc-13194282.creator: Derek J. Erstad, Zahra A. Fazal, Karlis Draulis, Feibi Zheng, Gretchen Jackson, Christy Y. Chai
pmc-13194282.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). To understand the value and experience of using the da Vinci 5 (dV-5) robotic surgical system among early-adopting surgeons in the United States. In March 2024, da Vinci 5 was released with new features such as a haptic technology (called Force Feedback) and Case Insights, a tool leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) to deliver video recordings of cases with objective metrics of performance. Few studies have assessed the value and challenges experienced by surgeons using this new system.

pmc-13217996.title: Development of a one-tube PAM-independent RCNPM platform using Cas12a for ultra-rapid simultaneous miR-499 and cTnT detection in early acute myocardial infarction diagnosis
pmc-13217996.creator: Jianguang Guo, Qingsong Wu, Fei Jiang, Meiling Cai, Linfeng Xie, Yuling Xie, Xinfan Lin, Xingfeng Chen, Siying Luo, Xiaofu Dai, Liangwan Chen
pmc-13217996.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAcute myocardial infarction (AMI) benefits from biomarkers and assays that support early triage. Cardiac troponin T (cTnT) is widely used, but may be less informative early after ischemia and can be elevated in non-AMI conditions. Circulating miR-499 has been reported to rise early after myocardial injury, yet miRNA detection is complicated by short target length and PAM constraints in many CRISPR-Cas12a designs.

pmc-13269984.title: Beyond Time Is Brain: The Time, Tissue, and Systems Framework for Acute Stroke
pmc-13269984.creator: Sonu Bhaskar
pmc-13269984.description: Acute ischaemic stroke care has long been guided by the maxim “time is brain,” yet outcome variability suggests that clock time alone is insufficient. We propose the Time, Tissue, and Systems (TTS) framework, a quantitative model integrating temporal progression, tissue vulnerability, and health-system performance.

pmc-13273590.title: Carbon balance zoning and carbon budget drivers for governance in the Chengdu Chongqing urban agglomeration
pmc-13273590.creator: Tonghui Yu, Binqian Dai, Xuan Zhu, Yu Zhang, Ran Xu, Xi Chen, Jiqiang Niu
pmc-13273590.description: SummaryAgainst China’s “dual-carbon” backdrop, identifying carbon balance patterns and governance zones in rapidly urbanizing regions is central to territorial spatial optimization. Using the Chengdu-Chongqing Urban Agglomeration as a case, this study develops a three-dimensional framework based on net carbon emissions, economic contribution, and ecological support coefficients to link carbon accounting, driver diagnosis, and zoning governance.
